caption: The drawing consists of four primary sections, all rendered in thin graphite lines on a yellowed, slightly stained paper background. In the upper left, a rectangular box labeled "TOP PLAN" displays a top-down view of a cabinet-like object, measured at 17 ½ inches in width and 4 ½ inches in depth, featuring four circular cut-outs. Below this, the "FRONT ELEVATION" shows a tall, rectangular clock case with decorative finials on top: three urn-shaped finials, the outer two on posts, and the central finial raised above two curving scrolls. A large circle in the upper part marks the position of a clock face, with a rectangular panel below it and a decorative base featuring three curved cutouts. In the lower right, the "SIDE ELEVATION" presents a narrow vertical rectangle, depicting the clock’s profile with one finial visible on top, a thick base, and subtle molding details. At the center right, “DETAIL OF HANDS” illustrates the minute and hour hands, elaborately shaped with pointed ends and decorative cutouts. In the upper center-right, text reads "TERRY SHELF CLOCK EARLY 19TH CENTURY," with a horizontal scale just below. The sheet is signed "Phillips" in the bottom right corner. The overall composition is symmetrical and technical, with labels and measured dimensions provided.
title: Clock
